correctness.rationale: For the rooted homogeneous b-ary tree, b>=2, geometric symbol r^depth with 0<r<1, T=Delta M_phi nabla initially on finitely supported vectors has diagonal matrix entry r^depth and strict-ancestor entry (r-1)r^(depth(v)-1). Its root row is an l2 functional iff br²<1; when it is, summing squared row masses yields the exact Hilbert–Schmidt norm [1+b(1-r)^2/(1-br²)]/(1-br²), hence compactness. The depthwise replication isometries and orthogonal complements W_k construct all wavelet angular chains, with d0=1, dk=(b-1)b^(k-1), on which T restricts to r^k times a single explicit upper-triangular A_{b,r}, diagonal r^i and upper entries (r-1)r^(j-1)b^((j-i)/2). Tail-row truncation gives exponential singular decay of A; direct-sum zeta yields Tr|T|^q=[(1-r^q)/(1-br^q)]Tr|A|^q and critical pole at q_c=log b/log(1/r), positive residue as claimed. Compression to level n and tail-rank approximation yield c j^{-gamma}<=s_j<=Cj^{-gamma}, gamma=log(1/r)/log b, proving the weak Schatten borderline and sharp threshold q>q_c. Independent finite tree matrices for (b,r,depth)=(2,0.5,4),(3,0.4,3) verified the kernel and partial Hilbert–Schmidt totals 3.5625<4 and 4.684288<5.9171597633, consistent with the exact infinite sums. Finite tests are corroboration, not the proof of the infinite decomposition.
